title: console-observability-triage-scratchpad-priya-2026-03-11
content:
Quick scratchpad for obs triage (morning). Informal notes, repro steps, actions.

Summary:
- Customer-reported slow dashboard load + blank widgets in Console (reported by Acme Corp, support ticket RT-1298).
- First seen 2026-03-10 ~22:40 UTC, intermittent until now. Appears correlated with spike in metrics ingestion (high cardinality series) and a failed rollup job on metrics pipeline.

What I saw (initial):
- Dashboard home: 3 out of 8 widgets empty (no data). Others show stale data (last point ~22:35).
- Browser devtools: 502 responses from /api/console/metrics/query for some queries.
- Kibana: query latency on metrics read cluster jumped from p50~120ms to p50~1.8s during spike.
- Ingestion logs (metrics-ingest-1): repeated backpressure warnings ~22:30-23:10, then rollup-job OBS-ROLLUP-02 failed due to OOM on collector pod.

Repro steps (local):
1) Login as an org admin (my test org) -> load Console -> click "Overview" -> observe load times.
2) Re-run offending query from network tab (copy request -> curl). Reproducible: some queries return 502, others succeed. Pattern: queries with GROUP BY high-cardinality tags fail.
3) Hitting metrics-read endpoint directly from k8s cluster (kubectl exec curl) returns 200 but slow (~1.5s) for same query.

Hypothesis:
- Root cause: rollup job OOM caused partial unavailability of rollups; ingestion backpressure increased load on read cluster (more raw time-series reads with higher cardinality), pushing read nodes to error on heavy GROUP BY queries.
- Secondary: client-side timeouts cause 502s surfaced to console; some widgets handle gracefully (show stale) while others bubble error.

Immediate mitigation (short-term):
- Restart rollup job collector (OBS-ROLLUP-02) with increased memory as hotfix (scale to 2x mem). -> ACTION: Eden to create hotfix pod config and deploy (PR referenced).
- Add temporary cache TTL increase on console widgets to avoid refetch under partial failure (reduce user-visible 502s). -> ACTION: Noah to patch frontend route to fallback to cached payload when read error >= 500.
- Rate-limit ad-hoc high-cardinality queries (circuit-breaker) on proxy layer for 12h. -> ACTION: Priya to add nginx rule to block heavy GROUP BY patterns (quick config).

Longer-term (postmortem candidates):
- Improve rollup job memory sizing and add OOM detector alert (OBS-ALERT-191).
- Add graceful degradation in console: show partial widget errors inline, plus specific callout explaining metrics ingestion issues (reduce CS tickets).
- Revisit cardinality control and query planner for read cluster; consider moving heavy GROUP BY to async jobs.

To-do / checklist (me):
- [x] Triage initial alert and confirm customer repro (Acme via RT-1298)
- [x] Capture network traces + curl payloads saved to /tmp/obs-traces-0311 (pushed to GH gist)
- [ ] Restart rollup collector with mem bump (coord with infra) -> waiting on Eden PR
- [ ] Deploy frontend cache fallback (noah) -> follow up in PR #613
- [ ] Add nginx rate-limit rule for heavy queries (temp) -> create MR
- [ ] Create postmortem doc skeleton (Confluence) -> assign owners
- [ ] Sync w/ CS on customer-facing note + ETA (Amy from CS owns comms)

Notes for handoff to SRE / infra:
- Collector pod logs show OOMKilled at 22:37 (pod metrics-collector-obs-02). Logs attached to OBS-4821. Suggest increase memory from 2Gi -> 4Gi and monitor for 1-2 days.
- Read cluster nodes show elevated CPU (90-95%) during incident window; may need short-term scale-up of read replica count.

Customer impact / timeline:
- 2026-03-10 22:30 UTC: first alert from synthetic tests (dashboard load failure).
- 2026-03-10 22:40 UTC: Acme ticket RT-1298 raised.
- 2026-03-10 23:15 UTC: Rollup job failed (OOM).
- 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC: partial recovery after manual pod restarts but still intermittent.

Slack notes (placeholders):
- #observability: thread pinned with initial findings (see OBS-4821).
- @ed en flagged infra scaling suggestion.

Questions / unresolved:
- Is there an automatic fallback if rollup job fails? (I think not currently).
- Do we have long-term limits on GROUP BY cardinality enforced at query layer? Need to check query-engine config.

Draft message to CS (short):
Hi Amy — quick update: we identified a metrics ingestion rollup job OOM that caused increased load on the read cluster and transient dashboard errors. We're deploying a hotfix (restart + mem bump) and a frontend fallback to reduce visible errors. ETA for hotfix: 2-4 hours. Will update once rollup is stable.

Next steps (today):
- 09:30 PT sync w/ Eden, Noah, Amy to align on hotfix + customer comms.
- land eden PR for collector mem bump -> monitor 1h post-deploy.

Raw links / artifacts saved:
- network logs gist: https://gist.github.com/priyad/obs-trace-0311
- collected curl payloads: /home/priya/obs/curl-requests-0311.txt
- support ticket: RT-1298 (zendesk)

Random notes to self (scratch):
- think about a lightweight synthetic that targets GROUP BY heavy queries to detect regressions earlier
- add a dashboard widget health-check alert (per-org) -> could reduce CS noise

End of scratchpad for now. Will convert to postmortem draft once hotfix is stable.
